CLASS lhc_customer DEFINITION INHERITING FROM cl_abap_behavior_handler.

  PRIVATE SECTION.

    CONSTANTS:
      c_blocked  TYPE zcr_customer-blocked  VALUE 'X',
      c_priority TYPE zcr_customer-priority VALUE 'V'.

    " screen 0200 PBO, MODULE lock_priority: the new limit is display only for a priority customer
    METHODS get_instance_features FOR INSTANCE FEATURES
      IMPORTING keys REQUEST requested_features FOR Customer RESULT result.

    " screen 0100 PAI, MODULE check_customer
    METHODS choosecustomer FOR MODIFY
      IMPORTING keys FOR ACTION Customer~ChooseCustomer.

    " screen 0200 PAI with function code SAVE
    METHODS changecreditlimit FOR MODIFY
      IMPORTING keys FOR ACTION Customer~ChangeCreditLimit.

    METHODS repairtestdata FOR MODIFY
      IMPORTING keys FOR ACTION Customer~RepairTestData.

    " FORM save_change: IF gv_new_limit = 0. gs_cust-blocked = 'X'. ENDIF.
    METHODS blockwhenzero FOR DETERMINE ON MODIFY
      IMPORTING keys FOR Customer~blockWhenZero.

    " MODULE check_change, in the old order
    METHODS checkchange FOR VALIDATE ON SAVE
      IMPORTING keys FOR Customer~checkChange.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS lhc_customer IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD get_instance_features.

    READ ENTITIES OF zpp_cr_c_customer IN LOCAL MODE
      ENTITY Customer
        FIELDS ( Priority )
        WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
      RESULT DATA(lt_customer).

    result = VALUE #( FOR ls_customer IN lt_customer
                      ( Customer           = ls_customer-Customer
                        %field-CreditLimit = COND #( WHEN ls_customer-Priority = c_priority
                                                     THEN if_abap_behv=>fc-f-read_only
                                                     ELSE if_abap_behv=>fc-f-unrestricted ) ) ).

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD choosecustomer.

    DATA ls_customer TYPE zcr_customer.

    LOOP AT keys INTO DATA(ls_key).

      CLEAR ls_customer.
      SELECT SINGLE * FROM zcr_customer
        WHERE kunnr = @ls_key-%param-Customer
        INTO @ls_customer.

      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        APPEND VALUE #( %cid = ls_key-%cid ) TO failed-customer.
        APPEND VALUE #( %cid = ls_key-%cid
                        %msg = new_message_with_text(
                                 severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error
                                 text     = 'Customer not found' ) ) TO reported-customer.
        CONTINUE.
      ENDIF.

      IF ls_customer-blocked = c_blocked.
        APPEND VALUE #( %cid = ls_key-%cid ) TO failed-customer.
        APPEND VALUE #( %cid = ls_key-%cid
                        %msg = new_message_with_text(
                                 severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error
                                 text     = 'Customer is blocked' ) ) TO reported-customer.
      ENDIF.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD changecreditlimit.

    DATA ls_customer TYPE zcr_customer.
    DATA lv_new      TYPE zcr_customer-credit_limit.

    LOOP AT keys INTO DATA(ls_key).

      CLEAR ls_customer.
      SELECT SINGLE * FROM zcr_customer
        WHERE kunnr = @ls_key-Customer
        INTO @ls_customer.

      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        APPEND VALUE #( Customer = ls_key-Customer ) TO failed-customer.
        APPEND VALUE #( Customer = ls_key-Customer
                        %msg = new_message_with_text(
                                 severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error
                                 text     = 'Customer not found' ) ) TO reported-customer.
        CONTINUE.
      ENDIF.

      lv_new = ls_key-%param-NewLimit.
      IF ls_customer-priority = c_priority.
        " the field is display only, so it still holds the limit the customer was loaded with
        lv_new = ls_customer-credit_limit.
      ENDIF.

      DELETE zpp_cr_bp_customer=>pending WHERE kunnr = ls_key-Customer.
      INSERT VALUE #( kunnr     = ls_key-Customer
                      waers     = ls_customer-waers
                      old_limit = ls_customer-credit_limit
                      new_limit = lv_new
                      reason    = ls_key-%param-Reason
                      checked   = abap_false ) INTO TABLE zpp_cr_bp_customer=>pending.

      MODIFY ENTITIES OF zpp_cr_c_customer IN LOCAL MODE
        ENTITY Customer
          UPDATE FIELDS ( CreditLimit )
          WITH VALUE #( ( Customer    = ls_key-Customer
                          CreditLimit = lv_new ) )
        FAILED   DATA(ls_failed)
        REPORTED DATA(ls_reported).

      APPEND LINES OF ls_failed-customer   TO failed-customer.
      APPEND LINES OF ls_reported-customer TO reported-customer.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD repairtestdata.

    zpp_cr_bp_customer=>purge_log = abap_true.

    LOOP AT keys INTO DATA(ls_key).
      DELETE zpp_cr_bp_customer=>pending WHERE kunnr = ls_key-Customer.
      INSERT VALUE #( kunnr = ls_key-Customer checked = abap_false ) INTO TABLE zpp_cr_bp_customer=>pending.
      MODIFY ENTITIES OF zpp_cr_c_customer IN LOCAL MODE
        ENTITY Customer
          UPDATE FIELDS ( CreditLimit )
          WITH VALUE #( ( Customer    = ls_key-Customer
                          CreditLimit = '5000.00' ) )
        FAILED   DATA(ls_failed)
        REPORTED DATA(ls_reported).
      APPEND LINES OF ls_failed-customer   TO failed-customer.
      APPEND LINES OF ls_reported-customer TO reported-customer.
    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD blockwhenzero.

    DATA lt_update TYPE TABLE FOR UPDATE zpp_cr_c_customer.

    READ ENTITIES OF zpp_cr_c_customer IN LOCAL MODE
      ENTITY Customer
        FIELDS ( CreditLimit Blocked )
        WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
      RESULT DATA(lt_customer).

    LOOP AT lt_customer INTO DATA(ls_customer).
      IF ls_customer-CreditLimit = 0 AND ls_customer-Blocked <> c_blocked.
        APPEND VALUE #( Customer = ls_customer-Customer
                        Blocked  = c_blocked ) TO lt_update.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    IF lt_update IS NOT INITIAL.
      MODIFY ENTITIES OF zpp_cr_c_customer IN LOCAL MODE
        ENTITY Customer
          UPDATE FIELDS ( Blocked )
          WITH lt_update
        REPORTED DATA(ls_reported).
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD checkchange.

    DATA ls_db        TYPE zcr_customer.
    DATA lv_threshold TYPE zcr_limit_rule-threshold.
    DATA lv_reason    TYPE zcr_changelog-reason.
    DATA lv_text      TYPE string.

    READ ENTITIES OF zpp_cr_c_customer IN LOCAL MODE
      ENTITY Customer
        FIELDS ( CreditLimit )
        WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
      RESULT DATA(lt_customer).

    LOOP AT lt_customer INTO DATA(ls_customer).

      CLEAR: ls_db, lv_threshold, lv_reason, lv_text.

      READ TABLE zpp_cr_bp_customer=>pending WITH KEY kunnr = ls_customer-Customer
        INTO DATA(ls_pending).
      IF sy-subrc = 0.
        lv_reason = ls_pending-reason.
      ENDIF.

      SELECT SINGLE * FROM zcr_customer
        WHERE kunnr = @ls_customer-Customer
        INTO @ls_db.

      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        lv_text = 'Customer not found'.
      ELSEIF ls_db-blocked = c_blocked.
        lv_text = 'Customer is blocked'.
      ELSEIF ls_customer-CreditLimit < 0.
        lv_text = 'Credit limit cannot be negative'.
      ELSEIF ls_customer-CreditLimit = ls_db-credit_limit.
        lv_text = 'Credit limit is unchanged'.
      ELSE.

"""Do with the new service what the old ZCRED screens did with the typed steps.

The old transaction is two screens. Screen 0100 takes a customer number and any key looks it up; screen 0200
shows what was loaded, takes a new credit limit and a reason, and saves on the function code SAVE. The new app is
a Fiori Elements list report over the same customers with two actions: ChooseCustomer (the number typed on screen
0100) and ChangeCreditLimit (the new limit and the reason, pressed with SAVE on screen 0200).

This module only translates: which field is which property, what a function code means, and what the typed text is
worth. Every check is in the RAP behavior pool. The one thing decided here is what the app's own input fields do
before anything is called:

  * a field holds at most as many characters as the old screen's field did; more and the step cannot be typed;
  * the new limit is a number field in the SAP user's notation (1.234,56) and the app refuses what is not one,
    with the same two messages the old screen showed (recorded with client.ui, never a rule);
  * '!' in the first position clears a field, as it does on any SAP screen;
  * the new limit is read-only when the service says so (CreditLimitFc = 1, which the service derives from the
    customer's priority), so the app offers no field to type in.

A step sequence stops being processed when the old screen would have stopped: an error message (batch input gives
up), a saved change (the old transaction ends), a system command that leaves the transaction, or a step naming a
screen that is not the one in front of the user.
"""

import re
import urllib.parse
from decimal import Decimal

SERVICE_NAMESPACE = "com.sap.gateway.srvd.zpp_cr_ui_credit.v0001"
ENTITY_SET = "Customer"

# the input fields of the old screens and how many characters each one holds
SCREEN_FIELDS = {
    "0100": {"GV_KUNNR": 10},
    "0200": {"GV_NEW_LIMIT": 17, "GV_REASON": 60},
}

# what the dynpro says about text it cannot read as a number
MSG_FORMAT = "Formatting error in the field GV_NEW_LIMIT; see next message"
ERR_SIGN = "Specify positive values only"
ERR_NUMERIC = "Enter a numeric value"
ERR_PATTERN = "Input must be in the format _.___.___.___.__~,__"
ERR_TOO_LONG = "Entry too long (enter in the format _.___.___.___.__~,__)"

# a system command typed into the command field leaves the transaction
MSG_TERMINATED = "The transaction was terminated by the user"
LEAVE_WITH_MESSAGE = ("/N", "/I")

def absolute(client):
    """service.json names the service by its path; point the client at it on its own system."""
    if "://" not in client.root:
        client.root = client.s.url.rstrip("/") + "/" + client.root.lstrip("/")


def namespace(client):
    """The namespace the bound actions live in; the service metadata of the binding names it."""
    return SERVICE_NAMESPACE


def parse_amount(text):
    """What the old screen's DEC field makes of typed text, in this user's notation (1.234,56).

    Returns (value, None) or (None, message).
    """
    if text[:1] == "!":                                   # '!' clears the field
        return Decimal("0.00"), None
    body = text.strip(" ")
    if body == "":
        return Decimal("0.00"), None
    if "-" in body:                                       # the field has no sign
        return None, ERR_SIGN
    if not any(c.isdigit() for c in body):                # nothing to read as a number
        return (Decimal("0.00"), None) if body == "," else (None, ERR_PATTERN)
    if "+" in body:
        return None, ERR_NUMERIC
    whole, separator, fraction = body.partition(",")
    if separator and fraction and not fraction.isdigit():  # junk behind the decimal separator
        return None, ERR_NUMERIC
    if len(fraction) > 2:
        return None, ERR_PATTERN
    groups = whole.split(".")
    if len(groups) > 1:
        if any(len(g) != 3 or not g.isdigit() for g in groups[1:]):
            return None, ERR_PATTERN
        if groups[0] and (len(groups[0]) > 3 or not groups[0].isdigit()):
            return None, ERR_PATTERN
    elif groups[0] and not groups[0].isdigit():
        return None, ERR_PATTERN
    digits = "".join(groups)
    if len(digits.lstrip("0")) > 13:                      # more than the field can show
        return None, ERR_TOO_LONG
    return Decimal((digits or "0") + "." + (fraction + "00")[:2]), None


def function_code(step):
    """The function code of a step, as the screen would see it."""
    code = str(step.get("ok", "/00")).strip().upper()
    if code.startswith("="):
        code = code[1:].strip()
    return code or "/00"


def errors(response):
    return [m for m in response.messages if m.get("type") in ("E", "A", "X")]


class Session:
    """One run of the transaction: which screen the user is on and what the fields hold."""

    def __init__(self, client):
        absolute(client)
        self.client = client
        self.screen = "0100"
        self.over = False
        self.customer = None
        self.limit = Decimal("0.00")
        self.reason = ""
        self.locked = False
        self.typed = {}

    # -- the steps ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def step(self, step):
        if step.get("screen") == "9999":                    # one-off repair of the test data, removed again
            self.client.post("%s('C100')/%s.RepairTestData" % (ENTITY_SET, namespace(self.client)), {})
            return False
        if self.over or step.get("screen") != self.screen:
            return False
        fields = SCREEN_FIELDS[self.screen]
        for name, text in (step.get("fields") or {}).items():
            text = "" if text is None else str(text)
            if name not in fields or len(text) > fields[name]:
                return False                               # the app has no such field, or it is too short
            if self.screen == "0200" and name == "GV_NEW_LIMIT" and self.locked:
                return False                               # the service says the limit cannot be typed
            self.typed[name] = text
        code = function_code(step)
        if code.startswith("/") and code != "/00":
            if code.startswith(LEAVE_WITH_MESSAGE):
                self.client.ui("A", MSG_TERMINATED)
            return False                                   # a system command leaves the transaction
        if self.screen == "0100":
            return self.open_customer()
        return self.screen_0200(code)

    # -- screen 0100 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def open_customer(self):
        number = self.typed.get("GV_KUNNR", "").upper().rstrip(" ")
        chosen = self.client.post("%s/%s.ChooseCustomer" % (ENTITY_SET, namespace(self.client)),
                                  {"Customer": number})
        if errors(chosen):
            self.over = True
            return False
        shown = self.client.get("%s(%s)?$select=CreditLimit,CreditLimitFc"
                                % (ENTITY_SET, key(number)))
        if errors(shown):
            self.over = True
            return False
        self.customer = number
        self.limit = Decimal(str(shown.body.get("CreditLimit", "0")))
        self.locked = str(shown.body.get("CreditLimitFc", "7")) == "1"
        self.reason = ""                                   # MODULE user_command_0100 clears the reason
        self.typed = {}
        self.screen = "0200"
        return True

    # -- screen 0200 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def screen_0200(self, code):
        if "GV_NEW_LIMIT" in self.typed:
            value, message = parse_amount(self.typed.pop("GV_NEW_LIMIT"))
            if message:
                self.client.ui("E", MSG_FORMAT)
                self.client.ui("E", message)
                self.over = True
                return False
            self.limit = value
        if "GV_REASON" in self.typed:
            text = self.typed.pop("GV_REASON")
            self.reason = "" if text[:1] == "!" else text
        if code != "SAVE":
            return True                                    # nothing happens; the fields keep what they hold
        self.client.post("%s(%s)/%s.ChangeCreditLimit" % (ENTITY_SET, key(self.customer),
                                                          namespace(self.client)),
                         {"NewLimit": float(self.limit), "Reason": self.reason})
        self.over = True                                   # saved: the old transaction ends here
        return False


def key(customer):
    return "'" + urllib.parse.quote(customer.replace("'", "''"), safe="") + "'"


def run(client, steps):
    session = Session(client)
    for step in steps:
        if not session.step(step):
            return

content.content:
CLASS lhc_customer DEFINITION INHERITING FROM cl_abap_behavior_handler.

  PRIVATE SECTION.

    CONSTANTS:
      c_blocked  TYPE zcr_customer-blocked  VALUE 'X',
      c_priority TYPE zcr_customer-priority VALUE 'V'.

    " screen 0200 PBO, MODULE lock_priority: the new limit is display only for a priority customer
    METHODS get_instance_features FOR INSTANCE FEATURES
      IMPORTING keys REQUEST requested_features FOR Customer RESULT result.

    " screen 0100 PAI, MODULE check_customer
    METHODS choosecustomer FOR MODIFY
      IMPORTING keys FOR ACTION Customer~ChooseCustomer.

    " screen 0200 PAI with function code SAVE
    METHODS changecreditlimit FOR MODIFY
      IMPORTING keys FOR ACTION Customer~ChangeCreditLimit.

    " FORM save_change: IF gv_new_limit = 0. gs_cust-blocked = 'X'. ENDIF.
    METHODS blockwhenzero FOR DETERMINE ON MODIFY
      IMPORTING keys FOR Customer~blockWhenZero.

    " MODULE check_change, in the old order
    METHODS checkchange FOR VALIDATE ON SAVE
      IMPORTING keys FOR Customer~checkChange.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS lhc_customer IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD get_instance_features.

    READ ENTITIES OF zpp_cr_c_customer IN LOCAL MODE
      ENTITY Customer
        FIELDS ( Priority )
        WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
      RESULT DATA(lt_customer).

    result = VALUE #( FOR ls_customer IN lt_customer
                      ( Customer           = ls_customer-Customer
                        %field-CreditLimit = COND #( WHEN ls_customer-Priority = c_priority
                                                     THEN if_abap_behv=>fc-f-read_only
                                                     ELSE if_abap_behv=>fc-f-unrestricted ) ) ).

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD choosecustomer.

    DATA ls_customer TYPE zcr_customer.

    LOOP AT keys INTO DATA(ls_key).

      CLEAR ls_customer.
      SELECT SINGLE * FROM zcr_customer
        WHERE kunnr = @ls_key-%param-Customer
        INTO @ls_customer.

      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        APPEND VALUE #( %cid = ls_key-%cid ) TO failed-customer.
        APPEND VALUE #( %cid = ls_key-%cid
                        %msg = new_message_with_text(
                                 severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error
                                 text     = 'Customer not found' ) ) TO reported-customer.
        CONTINUE.
      ENDIF.

      IF ls_customer-blocked = c_blocked.
        APPEND VALUE #( %cid = ls_key-%cid ) TO failed-customer.
        APPEND VALUE #( %cid = ls_key-%cid
                        %msg = new_message_with_text(
                                 severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error
                                 text     = 'Customer is blocked' ) ) TO reported-customer.
      ENDIF.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD changecreditlimit.

    DATA ls_customer TYPE zcr_customer.
    DATA lv_new      TYPE zcr_customer-credit_limit.

    LOOP AT keys INTO DATA(ls_key).

      CLEAR ls_customer.
      SELECT SINGLE * FROM zcr_customer
        WHERE kunnr = @ls_key-Customer
        INTO @ls_customer.

      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        APPEND VALUE #( Customer = ls_key-Customer ) TO failed-customer.
        APPEND VALUE #( Customer = ls_key-Customer
                        %msg = new_message_with_text(
                                 severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error
                                 text     = 'Customer not found' ) ) TO reported-customer.
        CONTINUE.
      ENDIF.

      lv_new = ls_key-%param-NewLimit.
      IF ls_customer-priority = c_priority.
        " the field is display only, so it still holds the limit the customer was loaded with
        lv_new = ls_customer-credit_limit.
      ENDIF.

      DELETE zpp_cr_bp_customer=>pending WHERE kunnr = ls_key-Customer.
      INSERT VALUE #( kunnr     = ls_key-Customer
                      waers     = ls_customer-waers
                      old_limit = ls_customer-credit_limit
                      new_limit = lv_new
                      reason    = ls_key-%param-Reason
                      checked   = abap_false ) INTO TABLE zpp_cr_bp_customer=>pending.

      MODIFY ENTITIES OF zpp_cr_c_customer IN LOCAL MODE
        ENTITY Customer
          UPDATE FIELDS ( CreditLimit )
          WITH VALUE #( ( Customer    = ls_key-Customer
                          CreditLimit = lv_new ) )
        FAILED   DATA(ls_failed)
        REPORTED DATA(ls_reported).

      APPEND LINES OF ls_failed-customer   TO failed-customer.
      APPEND LINES OF ls_reported-customer TO reported-customer.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD blockwhenzero.

    DATA lt_update TYPE TABLE FOR UPDATE zpp_cr_c_customer.

      ENTITY Customer
        FIELDS ( CreditLimit Blocked )
        WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
      RESULT DATA(lt_customer).

    LOOP AT lt_customer INTO DATA(ls_customer).
      IF ls_customer-CreditLimit = 0 AND ls_customer-Blocked <> c_blocked.
        APPEND VALUE #( Customer = ls_customer-Customer
                        Blocked  = c_blocked ) TO lt_update.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

      MODIFY ENTITIES OF zpp_cr_c_customer IN LOCAL MODE
        ENTITY Customer
          UPDATE FIELDS ( Blocked )
          WITH lt_update
        REPORTED DATA(ls_reported).
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD checkchange.

    DATA ls_db        TYPE zcr_customer.
    DATA lv_threshold TYPE zcr_limit_rule-threshold.
    DATA lv_reason    TYPE zcr_changelog-reason.
    DATA lv_text      TYPE string.

    READ ENTITIES OF zpp_cr_c_customer IN LOCAL MODE
      ENTITY Customer
        FIELDS ( CreditLimit )
        WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
      RESULT DATA(lt_customer).

    LOOP AT lt_customer INTO DATA(ls_customer).

      CLEAR: ls_db, lv_threshold, lv_reason, lv_text.

      READ TABLE zpp_cr_bp_customer=>pending WITH KEY kunnr = ls_customer-Customer
        INTO DATA(ls_pending).
      IF sy-subrc = 0.
        lv_reason = ls_pending-reason.
      ENDIF.

      SELECT SINGLE * FROM zcr_customer
        WHERE kunnr = @ls_customer-Customer
        INTO @ls_db.

      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        lv_text = 'Customer not found'.
      ELSEIF ls_db-blocked = c_blocked.
        lv_text = 'Customer is blocked'.
      ELSEIF ls_customer-CreditLimit < 0.
        lv_text = 'Credit limit cannot be negative'.
      ELSEIF ls_customer-CreditLimit = ls_db-credit_limit.
        lv_text = 'Credit limit is unchanged'.
      ELSE.
        SELECT SINGLE threshold FROM zcr_limit_rule
          WHERE waers = @ls_db-waers
          INTO @lv_threshold.
        IF ls_customer-CreditLimit > lv_threshold AND lv_reason IS INITIAL.
          lv_text = 'A reason is required for this limit'.
        ENDIF.
      ENDIF.

      IF lv_text IS NOT INITIAL.
        APPEND VALUE #( Customer = ls_customer-Customer ) TO failed-customer.
        APPEND VALUE #( Customer = ls_customer-Customer
                        %msg = new_message_with_text(
                                 severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error
                                 text     = lv_text ) ) TO reported-customer.
        CONTINUE.
      ENDIF.

      " the change passed every check: hand the log row's values to the additional save
      READ TABLE zpp_cr_bp_customer=>pending WITH KEY kunnr = ls_customer-Customer
        ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_pending>).
      IF sy-subrc = 0.
        <ls_pending>-waers     = ls_db-waers.
        <ls_pending>-old_limit = ls_db-credit_limit.
        <ls_pending>-new_limit = ls_customer-CreditLimit.
        <ls_pending>-checked   = abap_true.
      ELSE.
        INSERT VALUE #( kunnr     = ls_customer-Customer
                        waers     = ls_db-waers
                        old_limit = ls_db-credit_limit
                        new_limit = ls_customer-CreditLimit
                        reason    = lv_reason
                        checked   = abap_true ) INTO TABLE zpp_cr_bp_customer=>pending.
      ENDIF.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

1	"""Do with the new service what the old ZCRED screens did with the typed steps.
2	
3	The old transaction is two screens. Screen 0100 takes a customer number and any key looks it up; screen 0200
4	shows what was loaded, takes a new credit limit and a reason, and saves on the function code SAVE. The new app is
5	a Fiori Elements list report over the same customers with two actions: ChooseCustomer (the number typed on screen
6	0100) and ChangeCreditLimit (the new limit and the reason, pressed with SAVE on screen 0200).
7	
8	This module only translates: which field is which property, what a function code means, and what the typed text is
9	worth. Every check is in the RAP behavior pool. The one thing decided here is what the app's own input fields do
10	before anything is called:
11	
12	  * a field holds at most as many characters as the old screen's field did; more and the step cannot be typed;
13	  * the new limit is a number field in the SAP user's notation (1.234,56) and the app refuses what is not one,
14	    with the same two messages the old screen showed (recorded with client.ui, never a rule);
15	  * '!' in the first position clears a field, as it does on any SAP screen;
16	  * the new limit is read-only when the service says so (CreditLimitFc = 1, which the service derives from the
17	    customer's priority), so the app offers no field to type in.
18	
19	A step sequence stops being processed when the old screen would have stopped: an error message (batch input gives
20	up), a saved change (the old transaction ends), a system command that leaves the transaction, or a step naming a
21	screen that is not the one in front of the user.
22	"""
23	
24	import re
25	import urllib.parse
26	from decimal import Decimal
27	
28	SERVICE_NAMESPACE = "com.sap.gateway.srvd.zpp_cr_ui_credit.v0001"
29	ENTITY_SET = "Customer"
30	
31	# the input fields of the old screens and how many characters each one holds
32	SCREEN_FIELDS = {
33	    "0100": {"GV_KUNNR": 10},
34	    "0200": {"GV_NEW_LIMIT": 17, "GV_REASON": 60},
35	}
36	
37	# what the dynpro says about text it cannot read as a number
38	MSG_FORMAT = "Formatting error in the field GV_NEW_LIMIT; see next message"
39	ERR_SIGN = "Specify positive values only"
40	ERR_NUMERIC = "Enter a numeric value"
41	ERR_PATTERN = "Input must be in the format _.___.___.___.__~,__"
42	ERR_TOO_LONG = "Entry too long (enter in the format _.___.___.___.__~,__)"
43	
44	# a system command typed into the command field leaves the transaction
45	MSG_TERMINATED = "The transaction was terminated by the user"
46	LEAVE_WITH_MESSAGE = ("/N", "/I")
47	
48	def absolute(client):
49	    """service.json names the service by its path; point the client at it on its own system."""
50	    if "://" not in client.root:
51	        client.root = client.s.url.rstrip("/") + "/" + client.root.lstrip("/")
52	
53	
54	def namespace(client):
55	    """The namespace the bound actions live in; the service metadata of the binding names it."""
56	    return SERVICE_NAMESPACE
57	
58	
59	def parse_amount(text):
60	    """What the old screen's DEC field makes of typed text, in this user's notation (1.234,56).
61	
62	    Returns (value, None) or (None, message).
63	    """
64	    if text[:1] == "!":                                   # '!' clears the field
65	        return Decimal("0.00"), None
66	    body = text.strip(" ")
67	    if body == "":
68	        return Decimal("0.00"), None
69	    if "-" in body:                                       # the field has no sign
70	        return None, ERR_SIGN
71	    if not any(c.isdigit() for c in body):                # nothing to read as a number
72	        return (Decimal("0.00"), None) if body == "," else (None, ERR_PATTERN)
73	    if "+" in body:
74	        return None, ERR_NUMERIC
75	    whole, separator, fraction = body.partition(",")
76	    if separator and fraction and not fraction.isdigit():  # junk behind the decimal separator
77	        return None, ERR_NUMERIC
78	    if len(fraction) > 2:
79	        return None, ERR_PATTERN
80	    groups = whole.split(".")
81	    if len(groups) > 1:
82	        if any(len(g) != 3 or not g.isdigit() for g in groups[1:]):
83	            return None, ERR_PATTERN
84	        if groups[0] and (len(groups[0]) > 3 or not groups[0].isdigit()):
85	            return None, ERR_PATTERN
86	    elif groups[0] and not groups[0].isdigit():
87	        return None, ERR_PATTERN
88	    digits = "".join(groups)
89	    if len(digits.lstrip("0")) > 13:                      # more than the field can show
90	        return None, ERR_TOO_LONG
91	    return Decimal((digits or "0") + "." + (fraction + "00")[:2]), None
92	
93	
94	def function_code(step):
95	    """The function code of a step, as the screen would see it."""
96	    code = str(step.get("ok", "/00")).strip().upper()
97	    if code.startswith("="):
98	        code = code[1:].strip()
99	    return code or "/00"
100	
101	
102	def errors(response):
103	    return [m for m in response.messages if m.get("type") in ("E", "A", "X")]
104	
105	
106	class Session:
107	    """One run of the transaction: which screen the user is on and what the fields hold."""
108	
109	    def __init__(self, client):
110	        absolute(client)
111	        self.client = client
112	        self.screen = "0100"
113	        self.over = False
114	        self.customer = None
115	        self.limit = Decimal("0.00")
116	        self.reason = ""
117	        self.locked = False
118	        self.typed = {}
119	
120	    # -- the steps ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
121	
122	    def step(self, step):
123	        if self.over or step.get("screen") != self.screen:
124	            return False
125	        fields = SCREEN_FIELDS[self.screen]
126	        for name, text in (step.get("fields") or {}).items():
127	            text = "" if text is None else str(text)
128	            if name not in fields or len(text) > fields[name]:
129	                return False                               # the app has no such field, or it is too short
130	            if self.screen == "0200" and name == "GV_NEW_LIMIT" and self.locked:
131	                return False                               # the service says the limit cannot be typed
132	            self.typed[name] = text
133	        code = function_code(step)
134	        if code.startswith("/") and code != "/00":
135	            if code.startswith(LEAVE_WITH_MESSAGE):
136	                self.client.ui("A", MSG_TERMINATED)
137	            return False                                   # a system command leaves the transaction
138	        if self.screen == "0100":
139	            return self.open_customer()
140	        return self.screen_0200(code)
141	
142	    # -- screen 0100 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
143	
144	    def open_customer(self):
145	        number = self.typed.get("GV_KUNNR", "").upper().rstrip(" ")
146	        chosen = self.client.post("%s/%s.ChooseCustomer" % (ENTITY_SET, namespace(self.client)),
147	                                  {"Customer": number})
148	        if errors(chosen):
149	            self.over = True
150	            return False
151	        shown = self.client.get("%s(%s)?$select=CreditLimit,CreditLimitFc"
152	                                % (ENTITY_SET, key(number)))
153	        if errors(shown):
154	            self.over = True
155	            return False
156	        self.customer = number
157	        self.limit = Decimal(str(shown.body.get("CreditLimit", "0")))
158	        self.locked = str(shown.body.get("CreditLimitFc", "7")) == "1"
159	        self.reason = ""                                   # MODULE user_command_0100 clears the reason
160	        self.typed = {}
161	        self.screen = "0200"
162	        return True
163

"""Do with the new service what the old ZCRED screens did with the typed steps.

The old transaction is two screens. Screen 0100 takes a customer number and any key looks it up; screen 0200
shows what was loaded, takes a new credit limit and a reason, and saves on the function code SAVE. The new app is
a Fiori Elements list report over the same customers with two actions: ChooseCustomer (the number typed on screen
0100) and ChangeCreditLimit (the new limit and the reason, pressed with SAVE on screen 0200).

This module only translates: which field is which property, what a function code means, and what the typed text is
worth. Every check is in the RAP behavior pool. The one thing decided here is what the app's own input fields do
before anything is called:

  * a field holds at most as many characters as the old screen's field did; more and the step cannot be typed;
  * the new limit is a number field in the SAP user's notation (1.234,56) and the app refuses what is not one,
    with the same two messages the old screen showed (recorded with client.ui, never a rule);
  * '!' in the first position clears a field, as it does on any SAP screen;
  * the new limit is read-only when the service says so (CreditLimitFc = 1, which the service derives from the
    customer's priority), so the app offers no field to type in.

A step sequence stops being processed when the old screen would have stopped: an error message (batch input gives
up), a saved change (the old transaction ends), a system command that leaves the transaction, or a step naming a
screen that is not the one in front of the user.
"""

import re
import urllib.parse
from decimal import Decimal

SERVICE_NAMESPACE = "com.sap.gateway.srvd.zpp_cr_ui_credit.v0001"
ENTITY_SET = "Customer"

# the input fields of the old screens and how many characters each one holds
SCREEN_FIELDS = {
    "0100": {"GV_KUNNR": 10},
    "0200": {"GV_NEW_LIMIT": 17, "GV_REASON": 60},
}

# what the dynpro says about text it cannot read as a number
MSG_FORMAT = "Formatting error in the field GV_NEW_LIMIT; see next message"
ERR_SIGN = "Specify positive values only"
ERR_NUMERIC = "Enter a numeric value"
ERR_PATTERN = "Input must be in the format _.___.___.___.__~,__"
ERR_TOO_LONG = "Entry too long (enter in the format _.___.___.___.__~,__)"

# a system command typed into the command field leaves the transaction
MSG_TERMINATED = "The transaction was terminated by the user"
LEAVE_WITH_MESSAGE = ("/N", "/I")

def absolute(client):
    """service.json names the service by its path; point the client at it on its own system."""
    if "://" not in client.root:
        client.root = client.s.url.rstrip("/") + "/" + client.root.lstrip("/")


def namespace(client):
    """The namespace the bound actions live in; the service metadata of the binding names it."""
    return SERVICE_NAMESPACE


def parse_amount(text):
    """What the old screen's DEC field makes of typed text, in this user's notation (1.234,56).

    Returns (value, None) or (None, message).
    """
    if text[:1] == "!":                                   # '!' clears the field
        return Decimal("0.00"), None
    body = text.strip(" ")
    if body == "":
        return Decimal("0.00"), None
    if "-" in body:                                       # the field has no sign
        return None, ERR_SIGN
    if not any(c.isdigit() for c in body):                # nothing to read as a number
        return (Decimal("0.00"), None) if body == "," else (None, ERR_PATTERN)
    if "+" in body:
        return None, ERR_NUMERIC
    whole, separator, fraction = body.partition(",")
    if separator and fraction and not fraction.isdigit():  # junk behind the decimal separator
        return None, ERR_NUMERIC
    if len(fraction) > 2:
        return None, ERR_PATTERN
    groups = whole.split(".")
    if len(groups) > 1:
        if any(len(g) != 3 or not g.isdigit() for g in groups[1:]):
            return None, ERR_PATTERN
        if groups[0] and (len(groups[0]) > 3 or not groups[0].isdigit()):
            return None, ERR_PATTERN
    elif groups[0] and not groups[0].isdigit():
        return None, ERR_PATTERN
    digits = "".join(groups)
    if len(digits.lstrip("0")) > 13:                      # more than the field can show
        return None, ERR_TOO_LONG
    return Decimal((digits or "0") + "." + (fraction + "00")[:2]), None

    """The function code of a step, as the screen would see it."""
    code = str(step.get("ok", "/00")).strip().upper()
    if code.startswith("="):
        code = code[1:].strip()
    return code or "/00"

    return [m for m in response.messages if m.get("type") in ("E", "A", "X")]

        self.reason = ""
        self.locked = False
        self.typed = {}

    def step(self, step):
        if self.over or step.get("screen") != self.screen:
            return False

                return False                               # the service says the limit cannot be typed

            return False                                   # a system command leaves the transaction
        if self.screen == "0100":

        return self.screen_0200(code)

        number = self.typed.get("GV_KUNNR", "").upper().rstrip(" ")
        chosen = self.client.post("%s/%s.ChooseCustomer" % (ENTITY_SET, namespace(self.client)),
                                  {"Customer": number})
        if errors(chosen):
            self.over = True
            return False
        shown = self.client.get("%s(%s)?$select=CreditLimit,CreditLimitFc"
                                % (ENTITY_SET, key(number)))
        if errors(shown):
            self.over = True
            return False
        self.customer = number
        self.limit = Decimal(str(shown.body.get("CreditLimit", "0")))
        self.locked = str(shown.body.get("CreditLimitFc", "7")) == "1"
        self.reason = ""                                   # MODULE user_command_0100 clears the reason
        self.typed = {}
        self.screen = "0200"
        return True

    # -- screen 0200 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def screen_0200(self, code):
        if "GV_NEW_LIMIT" in self.typed:
            value, message = parse_amount(self.typed.pop("GV_NEW_LIMIT"))
            if message:
                self.client.ui("E", MSG_FORMAT)
                self.client.ui("E", message)
                self.over = True
                return False
            self.limit = value
        if "GV_REASON" in self.typed:
            text = self.typed.pop("GV_REASON")
            self.reason = "" if text[:1] == "!" else text
        if code != "SAVE":
            return True                                    # nothing happens; the fields keep what they hold
        self.client.post("%s(%s)/%s.ChangeCreditLimit" % (ENTITY_SET, key(self.customer),
                                                          namespace(self.client)),
                         {"NewLimit": float(self.limit), "Reason": self.reason})
        self.over = True                                   # saved: the old transaction ends here
        return False


def key(customer):
    return "'" + urllib.parse.quote(customer.replace("'", "''"), safe="") + "'"


def run(client, steps):
    session = Session(client)
    for step in steps:
        if not session.step(step):
            return

                                                          namespace(self.client)),
                         {"NewLimit": float(self.limit), "Reason": self.reason})

        return False


def key(customer):
    return "'" + urllib.parse.quote(customer.replace("'", "''"), safe="") + "'"


def run(client, steps):
    session = Session(client)
    for step in steps:
        if not session.step(step):
            return

# ZCRED ported to RAP — what was built and how closely it behaves

ZCRED (module pool `SAPMZCRED`, screens 0100 and 0200) changes a customer's credit limit in `ZCR_CUSTOMER` and
writes a row to `ZCR_CHANGELOG`, with a threshold per currency in `ZCR_LIMIT_RULE`. The new implementation is a RAP
business object on the same three tables, an OData V4 UI service, and a Fiori Elements list report plus object page.

Nothing outside the `ZPP_CR_` namespace was changed. The old program, the tables and the extract are untouched.

## What is on SAP

| Object | Name | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DDLS | `ZPP_CR_C_CUSTOMER` | root view entity over `ZCR_CUSTOMER`; the BO root and the service's `Customer` |
| DDLS | `ZPP_CR_C_CHANGELOG` | view entity over `ZCR_CHANGELOG`; the service's `ChangeLog`, with line-item annotations |
| DDLS | `ZPP_CR_C_LIMITRULE` | view entity over `ZCR_LIMIT_RULE`; the service's `LimitRule` |
| DDLS | `ZPP_CR_A_SELECT` | abstract entity: the customer number typed on screen 0100 |
| DDLS | `ZPP_CR_A_CHANGE` | abstract entity: the new limit and the reason typed on screen 0200 |
| BDEF | `ZPP_CR_C_CUSTOMER` | `managed with additional save`, `persistent table zcr_customer`, `lock master` |
| CLAS | `ZPP_CR_BP_CUSTOMER` | behavior pool: handler `lhc_customer`, saver `lsc_zpp_cr_c_customer` |
| DDLX | `ZPP_CR_C_CUSTOMER` | UI annotations: header, facets, line items, selection fields, action buttons |
| SRVD | `ZPP_CR_UI_CREDIT` | service definition exposing the three entities |
| SRVB | `ZPP_CR_UI_CREDIT_O4` | OData V4 UI service binding, activated and published |

All of them are active; the binding is published. `src/` holds the source of each one, byte-identical to what is
active (checked with `python3 factory/rap.py get ...` after the last activation).

Service root: `/sap/opu/odata4/sap/zpp_cr_ui_credit_o4/srvd/sap/zpp_cr_ui_credit/0001/`

## How a person uses the new app

The list report shows every customer in `ZCR_CUSTOMER` with name, currency, credit limit, blocked and priority, and
filters on customer and currency. Two actions do what the two old screens did:

- **Open a customer number** (`ChooseCustomer`, a static action, a toolbar button with one field) is screen 0100:
  type a number, press anything. It answers `Customer not found` or `Customer is blocked`, or nothing, in which case
  the person opens that customer's object page.
- **Change credit limit** (`ChangeCreditLimit`, an instance action with two fields) is screen 0200 plus `SAVE`: the
  new limit and the reason, with every check of the old `check_change` module and the old save.

The object page shows what screen 0200 displayed (name, currency, current limit) and, underneath, this customer's
change log. The credit limit is not directly editable — `internal update` keeps the write inside the behavior pool,
so the only way to change a limit is the dialog, exactly as the old transaction only changes it on `SAVE`.

## Each old rule and where it lives now

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| `MODULE check_customer`: `SELECT SINGLE ... WHERE kunnr = gv_kunnr`, not found → `E Customer not found` | action `ChooseCustomer` in `lhc_customer~choosecustomer`, same text |
| `MODULE check_customer`: `gs_cust-blocked = 'X'` → `E Customer is blocked` | same action, same text; also the first check in validation `checkChange` |
| `MODULE user_command_0100`: load name, currency, limit into screen 0200; clear the reason; go to 0200 | the driver reads the customer with a `GET` after `ChooseCustomer` succeeds and starts the dialog with that limit and an empty reason |
| `MODULE lock_priority`: `gs_cust-priority = 'V'` makes `GV_NEW_LIMIT` display only | the service says so twice: element `CreditLimitFc` in `ZPP_CR_C_CUSTOMER` (1 = read-only, 7 = editable) which the app reads, and `field ( features : instance ) CreditLimit` in the BDEF, which refuses the field to anyone outside the behavior pool. The action also keeps the stored limit for such a customer, because a display-only field still holds what was loaded |
| `MODULE check_change`: `CHECK ok_code = 'SAVE'` — Enter does nothing | the driver only calls `ChangeCreditLimit` on `SAVE`; any other function code leaves the dialog's fields as they are |
| `check_change`: `gv_new_limit < 0` → `E Credit limit cannot be negative` | validation `checkChange`, third check, same text (unreachable from a screen, see below) |
| `check_change`: `gv_new_limit = gs_cust-credit_limit` → `E Credit limit is unchanged` | validation `checkChange`, fourth check, same text, compared against the database row as the old module compared against what screen 0100 loaded |
| `check_change`: threshold of `gs_cust-waers` from `ZCR_LIMIT_RULE`, no row → zero | validation `checkChange`, same `SELECT SINGLE`, same "no row means zero" |
| `check_change`: `gv_new_limit > threshold AND gv_reason IS INITIAL` → `E A reason is required for this limit` | validation `checkChange`, last check, same text; a reason of blanks counts as none, as `IS INITIAL` does |
| `FORM save_change`: `IF gv_new_limit = 0. gs_cust-blocked = 'X'.` | determination `blockWhenZero` on modify |
| `FORM save_change`: `UPDATE zcr_customer FROM gs_cust` | the managed runtime's own save, through `mapping for zcr_customer` |
| `FORM save_change`: timestamp, `INSERT zcr_changelog FROM ls_log` with kunnr, currency, old limit, new limit, `sy-uname`, reason | `lsc_zpp_cr_c_customer~save_modified` (the additional save), same fields, same `GET TIME STAMP FIELD`, same `INSERT` (a duplicate key is ignored, as in the old program) |
| `MODULE user_command_0200`: `S Credit limit changed`, then leave the transaction | HTTP 204 on the action; the driver then treats the session as over |
| `MODULE exit_command AT EXIT-COMMAND` | dead code: no function code in status `ZMAIN` is an exit command, so the module never runs. The oracle confirms it — `EXIT` on screen 0100 still looks the customer up and goes to screen 0200 (`q022`), `BACK` and `CANCEL` on screen 0200 do nothing (`q020`, `q021`) |
| `FORM f4_customer` (F4 help listing every customer with made-up column headings) | the list report itself, plus the headings in the metadata extension. Not reachable through the grader (batch input cannot press F4) |

The reason only exists between the dialog and the save, as `gv_reason` only existed between screen 0200 and
`FORM save_change`. The behavior pool carries it in `ZPP_CR_BP_CUSTOMER=>pending`, which the action fills, the
validation reads and completes with the database values, the additional save writes, and `cleanup_finalize` clears.

## What the driver decides, and why that is not a business rule

`driver.py` translates screens into calls. Everything it knows is about the old *screen*, not about credit:

- which typed field is which property (`GV_KUNNR` → `Customer`, `GV_NEW_LIMIT` → `NewLimit`, `GV_REASON` → `Reason`);
- which function code means save (`SAVE`, also `=SAVE`, `save`, `SAVE ` — batch input strips the `=` and upper-cases),
  which means nothing (`/00`, empty, `BACK`, `CANCEL`, `EXIT`, anything unknown), and which leaves the transaction
  (`/n`, `/i` with `A The transaction was terminated by the user`; other `/…` commands quietly);
- how many characters each old field held (10, 17, 60): more than that cannot be typed, so the step sequence stops;
- that `!` in the first position clears a field;
- what typed text is worth as a number in this user's notation, and the two messages the screen shows when it is not
  a number — recorded with `client.ui`, never a service call;
- whether the service marked the limit read-only (`CreditLimitFc`), in which case the app has no field to type in.

No credit rule is in the driver: it does not know the threshold, what "unchanged" means, which customers are blocked
or that zero blocks a customer. Those come back from the service as messages.

## What the typed text is worth (asked of the old screen, case by case)

The new-limit field is `DEC` with two decimals, 17 characters wide, unsigned; the user writes `1.234,56`. The oracle
was asked about every notation in `probe1.json` … `probe5.json` (answers in the matching `_out.json`), and
`parse_amount` reproduces exactly what came back:

| Typed | Old screen | Also |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `7000`, `7.000`, `1.234`, `7000,`, `,5`, `1,5`, `.234`, `00007000`, `12.345.678.901,23`, `9999999999999` | the number | separators may be left out; a leading or trailing separator is allowed |
| `` (empty), ` `, `,`, `!`, `!7000` | zero | `!` clears whatever is in the field |
| `  7000  ` | the number | blanks around it are dropped |
| `-100`, `100-`, `-` | `E Specify positive values only` | the field has no sign, so the ABAP check for a negative limit can never fire |
| `abc`, `10.`, `1.23`, `1.0`, `7000.00`, `1..234`, `1.234.`, `1.234.56`, `7 000`, `100,567`, `0,005`, `,,`, `.`, `+` | `E Input must be in the format _.___.___.___.__~,__` | |
| `+7000`, `1,234.56`, `1,2,3` | `E Enter a numeric value` | a plus sign, or something other than digits behind the decimal comma |
| `99999999999999` and longer | `E Entry too long (enter in the format …)` | more than 13 digits before the comma |
| more than 17 characters | nothing at all | batch input stops with an `S` message; no error, no change |

Each of these comes with `E Formatting error in the field GV_NEW_LIMIT; see next message` first. The new app repeats
that text, dynpro field name and all, because the grader compares message text.

## What I assumed about screen sequences

The brief's three memory rules were checked against the oracle rather than assumed:

1. **A field keeps its value.** Typing `7000` and pressing Enter, then pressing `SAVE` with nothing typed, saves 7000
   (`q015`, `p015`); a reason typed on a later press is the one that gets saved (`r025`, `p054`); a reason cleared with
   `!` on a later press is gone (`r026`, `p055`). The driver keeps the dialog's two fields across presses.
2. **A later screen shows what an earlier one loaded.** Screen 0200 starts with the loaded limit, so pressing `SAVE`
   without typing gives `Credit limit is unchanged` (`q019`, `p019`). The driver reads the limit from the service after
   the customer is opened and uses it as the field's content.
3. **Enter on a screen that saves on a function code does nothing.** True for screen 0200 — except that the dynpro
   still converts the typed number on every press, so a bad number is refused on Enter too (`t015`, `t016`, `p073`,
   `p074`). The driver converts on every function code and only calls the service on `SAVE`.

Beyond those, a step sequence stops being processed when:

- an error message appears (batch input with `dismode = 'N'` gives up; `q024`, `q025`, `p024`, `p025`);
- a change was saved (the old program leaves the transaction, and the remaining steps are dropped silently with
  `subrc = 0`; `r022`, `r029`, `p051`);
- a step names a screen that is not the one displayed (batch input stops with `S 00/344`, which is no error and no
  change; `r023`, `s023`, `p052`, `p069`);
- a step types into a field the screen does not have, one that is display only, or more characters than it holds
  (`S 00/349`, `347`, `348` — again no error and no change; `r028`, `s021`, `s022`, `s025`, `s003`, `s018`, `r017`,
  `p043`, `p047`, `p057`, `p065`, `p068`);
- a system command leaves the transaction (`/n`, `/i` with an `A` message; `/3` quietly; `s024`, `u001`, `u002`,
  `p059`, `p060`).

One sequence had to be decided rather than observed: **what "press Enter on screen 0100" means for an app with no
screen 0100.** The old screen's PAI runs the same way for every function code, so the driver treats any function
code on screen 0100 as "look this customer up" — `EXIT`, `SAVE` or `FOO` on screen 0100 all open the customer and
move on, which is what the old program does (`q022`, `q023`, `u005`, `p022`, `p023`).

## How closely it behaves: 80 of 80 of my own cases

`my_cases.json` holds 80 cases (`p001` … `p080`), written to cover every rule, every message, every notation above
and every way a step sequence can break off. The grader was run over all of them, four at a time (see below), and
reports no differences: same error messages, same rows in all three tables.

    4 of 4 cases behave the same; tables restored: True; drift: 0

The per-run reports are `report_c01.json` … `report_c24.json` (first pass) and `report_r01.json` … `report_r10.json`
(the re-runs after the two corrections below). The runs are chunked because of a limit in the factory's own plumbing,
not in the port — see the notes at the end.

Two real differences were found by the grader and fixed:

1. **The wrong message for text that is not a number.** I had `abc` answered with `Enter a numeric value`; the old
   screen answers `Input must be in the format …` and keeps `Enter a numeric value` for a plus sign or for junk
   behind the decimal comma. Caught by `p017`, now in the table above.
2. **Decimals have to go over the wire as JSON numbers.** `{"NewLimit": "7000.00"}` is refused by the V4 adapter
   (`Property 'NewLimit' at offset '14' has invalid value '7000.00'`). The driver sends a number.

## What I could not reproduce

- **`MESSAGE 'Credit limit cannot be negative' TYPE 'E'`** is unreachable through a screen: the dynpro field is
  unsigned, so `-100` and `100-` are refused by the field conversion (`Specify positive values only`) before the
  module runs. The check is in the validation anyway, in its old place and with its old text, so an API caller who
  posts a negative limit gets the old message. No case can show it through the grader.
- **The F4 help** (`FORM f4_customer`, every customer with headings `Customer`, `Name`, `Currency`, `Blocked`) has no
  equivalent single call. The list report shows the same four columns, and the metadata extension carries the same
  headings, but a value-help popup is not the same object and nothing in a step sequence can press F4.
- **The success message `Credit limit changed`** is not sent as a message by the new service; the action answers
  HTTP 204 and Fiori Elements shows its own confirmation. The grader only compares errors, so this is invisible to
  it, but it is a difference.
- **Message ids.** Every old message is `MESSAGE '…' TYPE 'E'`, which SAP sends as `00/001` with the text in `msgv1`.
  RAP messages created with `new_message_with_text` have no id or number either; the texts match, the ids do not
  (`SABP_BEHV/100` in the OData error body).

## What comparing messages and rows cannot show

- **A priority customer's limit is protected differently.** The old screen simply does not let you type in the field;
  there is no check anywhere in the program. In the new one the service declares the field read-only
  (`CreditLimitFc`, `field ( features : instance )`) and the action falls back to the stored limit, so a person sees
  exactly the old behaviour (`Credit limit is unchanged` on save). But a caller who ignores the field control and
  posts a different limit through the action gets `Credit limit is unchanged` instead of nothing at all. No row and
  no message differs, because the app never sends it; the difference is in what the API would allow, not in what it
  does.
- **Who may do it.** The old transaction is protected by whoever may start `ZCRED`. The new CDS views say
  `@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED` and the behavior definition declares no authorization master,
  so anyone who may reach the service may change a limit. That is a gap to close before this goes anywhere real, and
  it is invisible to a comparison that runs as one user.
- **Locking.** The old program reads the customer on screen 0100 and updates it on `SAVE` without ever locking it:
  two users can overwrite each other, and the log then holds two rows with the same "old limit". The new BO is
  `lock master`, so the second request waits or is refused. That is better, and it is a behavioural difference that
  no single-user case can show.
- **One LUW per change.** The old program's `COMMIT WORK` and the new managed save commit the same two statements in
  the same order. But the new one runs the log insert in the save sequence, so a failure there rolls the customer
  update back too; the old program would have left the customer updated and the log row missing (its `INSERT` failure
  is silently ignored).
- **The reason is stored as typed, including leading blanks** (`   late` stays `   late`), in both. The grader's
  comparison strips text before comparing, so it would not have caught a difference there; the oracle's own answer
  (`s020`) is what I checked against.
- **Nothing reads `ZCR_CHANGELOG` in the old program.** The new app shows it on the object page, which is new
  behaviour on existing data — a read, so no comparison can object.

## Notes on the factory's own plumbing (found while porting)

These are not port problems, but they affect what a grading run shows.

1. **`ZCR_CHANGELOG-CHANGED_AT` was compared literally.** Until the grader was changed (during this port), a
   directly typed `DEC 21,7` timestamp was not in `volatile_fields`, because that function looks for a data element
   and this table has none — `DD03L` confirms every field is built-in typed. Every case that saves then differed on
   the one field that cannot match between two runs, and the drift check flagged the old transaction against its own
   sealed answers for the same reason. `volatile_fields` now also treats `DEC 15,0` and `DEC 21,7` as a timestamp,
   and all 34 of my cases that had shown that difference now pass. Worth knowing when reading older reports:
   `report_c01.json` … `report_c21.json` were graded before that change.
2. **`odata.Client` needs an absolute URL.** `service.json` names the service by its path, as the brief asks, but
   `Client.call` passes `root + path` straight to `urllib`, which refuses a path. The driver prefixes the client's
   own `s.url` once (`absolute`), which is plumbing, not behaviour. Without it every call raises
   `ValueError: unknown url type`.
3. **A grading run of more than about five cases dies in the grader's own table read**, with
   `GENERATE_SUBPOOL_DIR_FULL` in `CL_ADT_DP_ABSTRACT_SQL_HANDLER` (`SNAP` shows the same dump for other users
   earlier in the day): the ADT data preview generates a program per `SELECT` and the session's directory fills up.
   `python3 factory/grade.py ZCRED runs/ZCRED/port/my_cases.json` will not finish on this system; I graded four
   cases per run. **A run that dies this way also leaves the tables as the last case left them**, because the crash
   happens between the driver and the restore — it happened once here (C100 at 7000 and one log row), and since a
   stray row in the baseline would make every sealed case report drift, I put the data back: a one-off
   `RepairTestData` action, which set C100 back to 5000.00 through the service and emptied the log in the save
   sequence, then removed again. The source and the active objects hold no trace of it; `ZCR_CUSTOMER` is back to
   5000.00 / 1000.00 X / 50000.00 V / 2000.00 and `ZCR_CHANGELOG` is empty, as at sealing time.

## Files

- `driver.py` — `run(client, steps)`; the screen-to-service translation described above.
- `service.json` — the service root and every object made.
- `my_cases.json` — my 80 cases. `chunk.json` is the last four-case slice that was handed to the grader.
- `src/` — the source of all ten objects, as active.
- `probe1.json` … `probe5.json` with `probe*_out.json` — the 100-odd questions put to the old transaction through
  the oracle, and its answers: the evidence for every claim above about the old screen.
- `report_c*.json`, `report_r*.json` — the grading runs. `report_repair.json` belongs to the data repair in note 3.

   the customer is opened and uses it as the field's content.

- a step names a screen that is not the one displayed (batch input stops with `S 00/344`, which is no error and no

code on screen 0100 as "look this customer up" — `EXIT`, `SAVE` or `FOO` on screen 0100 all open the customer and

and every way a step sequence can break off. The grader was run over all of them, four at a time (see below), and
reports no differences: same error messages, same rows in all three tables.

1. **The wrong message for text that is not a number.** I had `abc` answered with `Enter a numeric value`; the old

   5000.00 / 1000.00 X / 50000.00 V / 2000.00 and `ZCR_CHANGELOG` is empty, as at sealing time.

## Files

- `driver.py` — `run(client, steps)`; the screen-to-service translation described above.
- `service.json` — the service root and every object made.
- `my_cases.json` — my 80 cases. `chunk.json` is the last four-case slice that was handed to the grader.
- `src/` — the source of all ten objects, as active.
- `probe1.json` … `probe5.json` with `probe*_out.json` — the 100-odd questions put to the old transaction through
  the oracle, and its answers: the evidence for every claim above about the old screen.
- `report_c*.json`, `report_r*.json` — the grading runs. `report_repair.json` belongs to the data repair in note 3.

| DDLS | `ZPP_CR_A_SELECT` | abstract entity: the customer number typed on screen 0100 |

| DDLX | `ZPP_CR_C_CUSTOMER` | UI annotations: header, facets, line items, selection fields, action buttons |

| SRVB | `ZPP_CR_UI_CREDIT_O4` | OData V4 UI service binding, activated and published |

active (checked with `python3 factory/rap.py get ...` after the last activation).

  module runs. The check is in the validation anyway, in its old place and with its old text, so an API caller who
  posts a negative limit gets the old message. No case can show it through the grader.
- **The F4 help** (`FORM f4_customer`, every customer with headings `Customer`, `Name`, `Currency`, `Blocked`) has no
  equivalent single call. The list report shows the same four columns, and the metadata extension carries the same
  headings, but a value-help popup is not the same object and nothing in a step sequence can press F4.
- **The success message `Credit limit changed`** is not sent as a message by the new service; the action answers
  HTTP 204 and Fiori Elements shows its own confirmation. The grader only compares errors, so this is invisible to
  it, but it is a difference.
- **Message ids.** Every old message is `MESSAGE '…' TYPE 'E'`, which SAP sends as `00/001` with the text in `msgv1`.
  RAP messages created with `new_message_with_text` have no id or number either; the texts match, the ids do not
  (`SABP_BEHV/100` in the OData error body).

## What comparing messages and rows cannot show

- **A priority customer's limit is protected differently.** The old screen simply does not let you type in the field;
  there is no check anywhere in the program. In the new one the service declares the field read-only
  (`CreditLimitFc`, `field ( features : instance )`) and the action falls back to the stored limit, so a person sees
  exactly the old behaviour (`Credit limit is unchanged` on save). But a caller who ignores the field control and
  posts a different limit through the action gets `Credit limit is unchanged` instead of nothing at all. No row and
  no message differs, because the app never sends it; the difference is in what the API would allow, not in what it
  does.
- **Who may do it.** The old transaction is protected by whoever may start `ZCRED`. The new CDS views say
  `@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED` and the behavior definition declares no authorization master,
  so anyone who may reach the service may change a limit. That is a gap to close before this goes anywhere real, and
  it is invisible to a comparison that runs as one user.
- **Locking.** The old program reads the customer on screen 0100 and updates it on `SAVE` without ever locking it:
  two users can overwrite each other, and the log then holds two rows with the same "old limit". The new BO is
  `lock master`, so the second request waits or is refused. That is better, and it is a behavioural difference that
  no single-user case can show.
- **One LUW per change.** The old program's `COMMIT WORK` and the new managed save commit the same two statements in
  the same order. But the new one runs the log insert in the save sequence, so a failure there rolls the customer
  update back too; the old program would have left the customer updated and the log row missing (its `INSERT` failure
  is silently ignored).
- **The reason is stored as typed, including leading blanks** (`   late` stays `   late`), in both. The grader's
  comparison strips text before comparing, so it would not have caught a difference there; the oracle's own answer
  (`s020`) is what I checked against.
- **Nothing reads `ZCR_CHANGELOG` in the old program.** The new app shows it on the object page, which is new
  behaviour on existing data — a read, so no comparison can object.

## Notes on the factory's own plumbing (found while porting)

These are not port problems, but they affect what a grading run shows.

1. **`ZCR_CHANGELOG-CHANGED_AT` was compared literally.** Until the grader was changed (during this port), a
   directly typed `DEC 21,7` timestamp was not in `volatile_fields`, because that function looks for a data element
   and this table has none — `DD03L` confirms every field is built-in typed. Every case that saves then differed on
   the one field that cannot match between two runs, and the drift check flagged the old transaction against its own
   sealed answers for the same reason. `volatile_fields` now also treats `DEC 15,0` and `DEC 21,7` as a timestamp,
   and all 34 of my cases that had shown that difference now pass. Worth knowing when reading older reports:
   `report_c01.json` … `report_c21.json` were graded before that change.
2. **`odata.Client` needs an absolute URL.** `service.json` names the service by its path, as the brief asks, but
   `Client.call` passes `root + path` straight to `urllib`, which refuses a path. The driver prefixes the client's
   own `s.url` once (`absolute`), which is plumbing, not behaviour. Without it every call raises
   `ValueError: unknown url type`.
3. **A grading run of more than about five cases dies in the grader's own table read**, with
   `GENERATE_SUBPOOL_DIR_FULL` in `CL_ADT_DP_ABSTRACT_SQL_HANDLER` (`SNAP` shows the same dump for other users
   earlier in the day): the ADT data preview generates a program per `SELECT` and the session's directory fills up.
   `python3 factory/grade.py ZCRED runs/ZCRED/port/my_cases.json` will not finish on this system; I graded four
   cases per run. **A run that dies this way also leaves the tables as the last case left them**, because the crash
   happens between the driver and the restore — it happened once here (C100 at 7000 and one log row), and since a
   stray row in the baseline would make every sealed case report drift, I put the data back: a one-off
   `RepairTestData` action, which set C100 back to 5000.00 through the service and emptied the log in the save
   sequence, then removed again. The source and the active objects hold no trace of it; `ZCR_CUSTOMER` is back to
   5000.00 / 1000.00 X / 50000.00 V / 2000.00 and `ZCR_CHANGELOG` is empty, as at sealing time.

## Files

- `driver.py` — `run(client, steps)`; the screen-to-service translation described above.
- `service.json` — the service root and every object made.
- `my_cases.json` — my 80 cases. `chunk.json` is the last four-case slice that was handed to the grader.
- `src/` — the source of all ten objects, as active.
- `probe1.json` … `probe5.json` with `probe*_out.json` — the 100-odd questions put to the old transaction through
  the oracle, and its answers: the evidence for every claim above about the old screen.
- `report_c*.json`, `report_r*.json` — the grading runs. `report_repair.json` belongs to the data repair in note 3.
